arrival.note: Not_later_than precision, and the date is the date of his own advertisement in the Chicago Democrat - a man advertising a tavern stand in Chicago on 4 October 1833 was in Chicago on 4 October 1833. When he actually came is not stated.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1833-10-04 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. reason_for_coming.note: His own advertisement describes the stand as 'lately occupied by Mr. Wm. W. Wattles', which is a succession, not a founding.

lives_at.note: The building record has his tenancy running 1834-1837, which covers the scene date, and a landlord of this period lived in his house. Inferred rather than documented because the tenancy dates are the building record's reading of two sources that do not agree about who opened the house.

works_at.note: Both sources behind the building record put Ingersoll in the Green Tree across 1835.

present_on_scene_date.note: A tenancy given as 1834-1837 covers 1 July 1835; no source states his whereabouts on that day.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

persons.name: Chester Ingersoll

associated_with.note: GROUND HE BOUGHT, WHICH IS NOT GROUND HE STOOD ON — the rung is `tract` for that reason, and `land_purchased` is in neither the home kinds nor the work kinds because a holding is not a place a man was. The federal tract-sale register carries 1 row(s) — ls0246 — to this purchaser, read as 'INGERSOLL CHESTER', sorted onto school_section by tools/sort_land_sales_onto_tracts.py and covering about 2.25 acre(s) of it. THE TIER IS INFERRED AND THE TWO HALVES DIFFER: the purchase is documented — the register is a public record and states it — while the tie between that purchaser and THIS card is an identity ruling, upheld under T-0850 on 2026-09-10 by the rule 'INGERSOLL CHESTER matches Chester Ingersoll: the forename names Chester Ingersoll of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full.'. The weaker half sets the tier. `to` is null because the register records a sale and not a tenure.

occupation.note: Landlord of the Green Tree Tavern 1834-1837 per this project's building record, and before that of the old Wolf Point house which he re-christened 'The Travelers' Home'. The Democrat of 26 November 1833 carries his own advertisement, dated 4 October 1833, for a tavern stand 'lately occupied by Mr. Wm. W. Wattles'.

workplaces.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card ingersoll_chester (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED RESIDENT IN A CONTEMPORARY NEWSPAPER, which is worth more than any amount of Andreas. Two further things fix him in the town in this period: his house was the district polling place on 9 December 1833, and a travelling ventriloquist named Kenworthy advertised in the Democrat of 10 June 1834 the close of an engagement at 'the Travelers' Home, a hotel kept by Chester Ingersoll, on Wolf Point'. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “INGERSOLL CHESTER”, 1833-10-24 to 1835-06-26: 1 federal land entry — SW sec 28 T39N R13E and 1 parcel of the school section — BL37 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read, 163.79 acres stated in all, for $253.10 (ls0246, ls0849). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: INGERSOLL CHESTER matches Chester Ingersoll: the forename names Chester Ingersoll of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('ingersoll_chester:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: A TAVERN KEEPER WHO MOVED HOUSE INSIDE THE DATASET'S OWN WINDOW, which is why the two buildings he is attached to must not be collapsed. In 1833-34 he kept the old Wolf Point house under the sign of the Travelers' Home; by the scene date this project's building record has him at the Green Tree. Both are in data/structures/ and only the second is linked here. THE ARRIVAL IS A NEWSPAPER DATE, NOT A JOURNEY: 4 October 1833 is when his copy was dated, and it bounds his arrival from above and not at all from below.
